 Beloved newsreader dies as devastated fans pay tribute to 'true gentleman'
 Megan Bull Updated 2026년 10월 28일 수 오전 9:10 UTC 2 Jim Boyd's death was announced on WCVB on Tuesday (Image: Getty) Beloved Boston newsreader Jim Boyd has died at the age of 84. A longtime anchor at WCVB-TV, the station confirmed his passing on Tuesday (27 October). His cause of death has not been shared. He is survived by his wife, Linda, and their three daughters. "We have some really sad news to share this evening," journalist Maria Stephanos said live on air. "Former Newscenter Five anchor and a true gentleman, Jim Boyd has died." Issuing a heartfelt tribute to the broadcaster, who worked for the network for almost 40 years, the programme included an interview with Boyd's's former co-anchor, Susan Wornick. Reflecting on their "enduring friendship," she noted that they'd kept in touch after his retirement.
 Born in 1942, Boyd started his career in the mailroom at WNET-TV in New York in 1961, before joining WCVB as a general assignment reporter in 1972.
 After moving to the station, the TV star eventually became an anchor on the news desk and spent almost 40 years reporting on the latest developments across New England and Boston. As a result, he was inducted into the Massachusetts Broadcasters Hall of Fame.
 Boyd, who officially retired in 2008, spent the next few years working towards a bachelor's degree in sociology at Tufts University, which he eventually earned in 2013.
 According to IMDb, he also appeared in various films, including The Equaliser, The Judge and Spotlight.
 In recognition of his esteemed career, Boyd received several awards, including a Golden Circle Award from the National Academy of Television Arts and Sciences (New England chapter).
 Following the news of Boyd's death, tributes have poured in from fans. Responding to an announcement posted by WCVB on Instagram, one wrote: "Worked with Jim many times. A true journalist and gentleman. RIP Jim."
 "Sending my love to the Boyd family and the WCVB family; he and Susan Wornick were an iconic midday duo!" noted a second.
 Meanwhile, a third commented, "Oh my. He was a class act and consummate professional. I watched the midday news with him and Susan daily for many years. Condolences to the Boyd family. He truly was one of a kind."
 "He was a class act! One of the best! Rest in peace..." added a fourth.
